Ecstatic

ek-STAT-ik -- stress on the second syllable, STAT. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ecstatic is full of overwhelming joy.

The whole village was ecstatic when the home team carried the national trophy down Main Street for the first time.

Worked Example

The shelter door opens, his lost dog bounds straight into his arms, and the boy laughs and cries at the same time, spinning them both in circles.

Joy that overwhelming -- too big for a smile, spilling out as laughter, tears, and spinning -- is what ecstatic means. It sits far above 'happy' or 'pleased' on the joy scale.

How Ecstatic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

overjoyed

overjoyed: extremely happy

thrilled

thrilled: very excited and pleased

euphoric

euphoric: swept up in intense, almost floating happiness

Antonyms

miserable

miserable: deeply unhappy

despondent

despondent: in very low spirits, without hope

How Strong Is It? — thrilled → ecstatic → euphoric

thrilled vs. ecstatic

thrilled vs. ecstatic: Thrilled is strong but still a rung below ecstatic -- a thrilled winner beams and cheers, while an ecstatic one is beside themselves, joy overflowing beyond any control.

euphoric vs. ecstatic

euphoric vs. ecstatic: Euphoric matches or even tops ecstatic: ecstatic describes overwhelming joy at something, while euphoric describes a wave of happiness so intense the whole world seems to float.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — sta-/stas-

root — sta-/stas-: to stand (Greek ekstasis 'a standing outside oneself,' from ek- 'out' + histanai 'to stand')

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: having the characteristics of; like (Greek -ikos, via Latin -icus)

Put it together

Put it together: Ecstatic comes from Greek ekstasis, 'a standing outside oneself' -- ek- ('out') plus histanai ('to stand'). Joy this big pushes you right out of your ordinary self: when you are ecstatic, you are quite literally 'beside yourself' with happiness.

Use the root in a new word: stationary

Use the root in a new word: stationary: The traffic sat completely stationary for an hour after the parade closed Main Street.

Root Check

Word Choice

Save ecstatic for the top of the joy scale -- news that makes people scream, dance, or cry happy tears. It often appears as 'absolutely ecstatic' and takes 'about' or 'at': ecstatic about the results, ecstatic at the news.
